Electrical and Pneumatic Lockout guide

What Is Plug and Pneumatic Connection Lockout?

Golden ruleUnplugging a plug is not isolation on its own; maintenance must not begin until the plug has been locked out and tagged.

Plug and pneumatic connection lockout equipment are LOTO devices that prevent plug-connected electrical devices and pneumatic tools connected to an air line from being re-energized during maintenance. The plug or quick-connect end is enclosed in a lockable housing; when the housing is closed with a safety padlock, the plug cannot be inserted into the socket and the hose cannot be connected to the air line.

A significant share of the equipment most often taken for maintenance in workshops and production lines is plug-in machines and pneumatic tools. Pulling the plug may seem practical, but another worker who is unaware of the situation may plug it back in. A plug lockout physically eliminates that possibility; on pneumatic lines, residual pressure must be released before locking out.

At Sofilx, we offer lockout equipment for small electrical plugs, industrial plugs, combination electrical and pneumatic connections, gas cylinders and air sources, as well as a plug lockout bag.

Buying guide

How to Choose the Right Plug and Pneumatic Lockout Equipment?

Check these criteria before ordering. If you are unsure, send a photo and we will choose together.

Ask an expert
  • Plug size: Measure the widest part of the plug; the plug should fit into the housing without being forced.
  • Connection type: Clarify whether the equipment will be used for electrical only, pneumatic only, or both.
  • Pressure release: On pneumatic and gas lines, always bleed off residual pressure in the line before locking out.
  • Padlock and tag: Close the housing with a safety padlock and hang a warning tag on it showing who locked it out and why.
  • Multiple users: If more than one person will work, add a lockout hasp to the enclosure so everyone can attach their own lock.
  • Line isolation: If you need to isolate the entire compressed air line, use the air supply lockout together with valve lockouts.
Applications

Where Is Plug and Pneumatic Lockout Equipment Used?

Workshops

Used to prevent plug-in benchtop machines and hand tools from being restarted during maintenance and repair.

Pneumatic lines

Prevents pneumatic tools and quick-connect points from being connected to the air line during maintenance.

Production and assembly lines

Provides safety when cleaning and maintaining plug-in and pneumatically controlled machines in the automotive and assembly industries.

Construction sites and field work

Prevents unauthorized use of welding machines, cable reels and gas cylinders.

Frequently asked questions

About Electrical and Pneumatic Lockout

If you could not find the answer you are looking for, message us on WhatsApp and we will determine the right model together.

Ask on WhatsApp
Isn't unplugging the equipment enough before maintenance?
No. A plug that has been pulled can be plugged back in by someone unaware of the situation. When the plug is locked and tagged, this risk is eliminated.
How much does plug and pneumatic lockout equipment cost?
Prices vary by model, size and order quantity. For a current quote, you can message the product code and quantity to our WhatsApp line or call us by phone.
Are there suitable models for which plug types?
Models are available for sizes from small single-phase plugs to industrial socket plugs; for very large plugs, the BD-D71 plug lockout bag can be used.
How is a pneumatic connection locked out?
First the pressure in the line is released, then the quick-connect end is placed inside the lockout device and the device is closed with a padlock. An air source or valve lockout can also be added for the whole line.
Can more than one person attach a lock to the same plug lockout?
Yes, when a lockout hasp is added to the housing, each worker can fit their own padlock.
Can gas cylinders be locked out too?
Yes. The adjustable BD-Q31 and plastic-bodied BD-Q21 models are used to block access to cylinder and tank valves.
Does a plug lockout provide full protection against electric shock?
A plug lockout protects the person doing maintenance by preventing the device from being re-energized; even so, you must verify that the device is de-energized before starting work.
